about: The Dalmore stands on the north shore of the Cromarty Firth at Alness, in the northern Highlands. It was founded in 1839 and from the 1860s was run by the Mackenzie family, whose clan crest, a royal stag with twelve points, still appears on every bottle. Clan legend holds that a Mackenzie ancestor saved King Alexander III from a charging stag in 1263 and was granted the stag as his emblem. The distillery is now part of Whyte & Mackay.

Dalmore’s stills are unusual, with flat-topped wash stills and spirit stills cooled by copper water jackets, which favor a rich, weighty spirit. The 12 Year Old spends its first nine years in American white oak ex-bourbon casks. Half is then moved into casks that held 30-year-old Matusalem oloroso sherry from González Byass, the other half stays in bourbon wood, and after three more years the two are married and bottled at 40%. Published tasting notes point to Seville orange, chocolate, spiced fruitcake and vanilla, with a long, fruity finish.
facts: 9 years ex-bourbon American oak; half then 3 years in 30-year-old Matusalem oloroso sherry casks
